audits.title: Methodological issues in the use of guidelines and audit to improve clinical effectiveness in breast cancer in one United Kingdom health region.
audits.standard: Regional evidence-based breast cancer clinical guidelines and guideline targets
audits.setting: North Thames (East) Health region: 21 acute hospitals and 16 specialist surgeons treating breast cancer (Thames Cancer Registry)

cycle1.result: Chemotherapy use 17% and axillary surgery 46% (previous studies in this population).

audits.intervention: Regional guidelines, senior clinicians as local leads, audit of quality, clinician ownership of data, confidential feedback to participants and education.

cycle2.result: Chemotherapy use rose to 23% and axillary surgery to 76%.

audits.other_findings: The audit sample was 28% of breast cancers diagnosed in the region in 1992; the pilot led to prospective audit of all regional breast cancers and a 15-fold increase in high-quality clinical information.
audits.citation: Bell CM, Ma M, Campbell S, Basnett I, Pollock A, Taylor I. Methodological issues in the use of guidelines and audit to improve clinical effectiveness in breast cancer in one United Kingdom health region. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2000;26(2):130-136. doi:10.1053/ejso.1999.0755. PMID: 10744929.

audits.title: Implementing clinical practice guidelines: a community-based audit of breast cancer treatment. Australian Capital Territory and South Eastern New South Wales Breast Cancer Treatment Group.
audits.standard: Four locally agreed guidelines based on 1995 NHMRC breast cancer guidelines
audits.setting: Breast cancer treatment facilities and practices in the ACT and South Eastern New South Wales

cycle1.result: 85/87 (98%) had radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery; 95/99 (96%) indicated received systemic adjuvant therapy; all 27 women under 50 with node-positive disease received chemotherapy; axillary surgery in 173 (91%).

audits.other_findings: Audit programme with clinician and consumer support was used to enhance guideline uptake.
audits.citation: Craft PS, Zhang Y, Brogan J, Tait N, Buckingham JM. Implementing clinical practice guidelines: a community-based audit of breast cancer treatment. Australian Capital Territory and South Eastern New South Wales Breast Cancer Treatment Group. Med J Aust. 2000;172(5):213-216. doi:10.5694/j.1326-5377.2000.tb123911.x. PMID: 10776392.

audits.title: Adjuvant systemic therapies in women with breast cancer: an audit of clinical practice in Italy.
audits.standard: International Consensus Panel recommendations for adjuvant systemic therapy

cycle1.result: Endocrine therapy not given to 102/541 (19%) endocrine-responsive patients; given to 22/182 (12%) endocrine-unresponsive patients; chemotherapy prescribed for 98%.

audits.other_findings: CMF used in 453/754 (60%) and anthracyclines in 253/754 (34%).
audits.citation: Roila F, Ballatori E, Patoia L, Palazzo S, Veronesi A, Frassoldati A, et al.. Adjuvant systemic therapies in women with breast cancer: an audit of clinical practice in Italy. Ann Oncol. 2003;14(6):843-848. doi:10.1093/annonc/mdg256. PMID: 12796020.

audits.title: Audit of compliance to adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy guidelines in breast cancer in a cancer network.
audits.standard: North Trent Cancer Network Breast Group adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy guidelines (revised 1998)
audits.setting: North Trent Cancer Network cancer units and cancer centre

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 82% (chemotherapy 90%, radiotherapy 74%), similar across the network; compliance undetermined in 5%.

audits.other_findings: On case review 22% of non-compliant incidents were justified and 16% reflected variation in guideline interpretation.
audits.citation: Balasubramanian SP, Murrow S, Holt S, Manifold IH, Reed MW. Audit of compliance to adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy guidelines in breast cancer in a cancer network. Breast. 2003;12(2):136-141. doi:10.1016/s0960-9776(02)00263-1. PMID: 14659343.

audits.title: National breast cancer audit: overview of invasive breast cancer management.
audits.setting: National Breast Cancer Audit, 274 participating breast surgeons in Australia and New Zealand

cycle1.result: Breast-conserving surgery stable at 60%; margins involved in 5% with a further 9% under 1 mm; radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery 86%; tamoxifen in 83% of ER-positive cases; chemotherapy in 78% of ER-negative node-positive postmenopausal patients.

audits.other_findings: Radiotherapy after mastectomy in 71% with tumours over 5 cm and 75% with four or more positive nodes; margins and tamoxifen use in ER-negative cancers flagged for improvement.
audits.citation: Cuncins-Hearn AV, Boult M, Babidge W, Zorbas H, Villanueva E, Evans A, et al.. National breast cancer audit: overview of invasive breast cancer management. ANZ J Surg. 2006;76(8):745-750. doi:10.1111/j.1445-2197.2006.03846.x. PMID: 16916399.

audits.title: Audit system on quality of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment (QT): results from the survey on screen-detected lesions in Italy, 2004.
audits.standard: Recommendations on screen-detected breast lesion diagnosis and treatment (waiting times, frozen section, specimen X-ray, pre-operative diagnosis)

cycle1.result: Generally good quality with an improving trend; sentinel node technique used in almost 70% of screen-detected invasive cancers.

audits.other_findings: Waiting times, frozen section on small lesions and specimen X-ray compliance were critical issues.
audits.citation: Ponti A, Mano MP, Distante V, Baiocchi D, Bordon R, Federici A, et al.. Audit system on quality of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment (QT): results from the survey on screen-detected lesions in Italy, 2004. Epidemiol Prev. 2007;31(2-3 Suppl 2):69-75. PMID: 17824364.

audits.standard: Breast screening quality indicators and recommendations
audits.setting: Italian Breast Screening Network (GISMa) data on screen-detected lesions

cycle1.result: Overall good quality; preoperative diagnosis reached acceptable target with regional variation; sentinel node used in over 70% of invasive cancers.

audits.title: Enhancing the quality of care for patients with breast cancer: seven years of experience with a Dutch auditing system.
audits.standard: Dutch National Guideline for breast cancer; nine quality indicators including maximum waiting times

cycle1.result: Preoperative MDT discussion 56%, postoperative 70%; outpatient waiting time met 61%, diagnosis 82%, surgery 34%; successful sentinel node 69%.

audits.intervention: Intervention project in 2004 and 2005 to improve efficiency of diagnosis and surgical treatment.

cycle2.result: Preoperative MDT 83%, postoperative 98%; waiting times 74%, 92% and 52%; sentinel node 92%; >10 nodes in ALND 85%; single operation 87%; discharge within 7 days 98%.

audits.other_findings: All nine indicators improved significantly over seven years.
audits.citation: Veerbeek L, van der Geest L, Wouters M, Guicherit O, Does-den Heijer A, Nortier J, et al.. Enhancing the quality of care for patients with breast cancer: seven years of experience with a Dutch auditing system. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2011;37(8):714-718. doi:10.1016/j.ejso.2011.03.003. PMID: 21458947.

audits.title: National Breast Cancer Audit: overview of invasive breast cancer in New Zealand.
audits.standard: National Breast Cancer Audit performance indicators and clinical guidelines
audits.setting: National Breast Cancer Audit, New Zealand data

cycle1.result: 3% involved margins; 72% of screening and 86% of symptomatic high-risk patients did not receive post-mastectomy radiotherapy; endocrine therapy prescribed to 81% of hormone receptor positive patients.

audits.other_findings: 62% of BreastScreen patients had sentinel node biopsy alone; higher breast conservation in screened patients.
audits.citation: Ooi CW, Campbell ID, Kollias J, de Silva P. National Breast Cancer Audit: overview of invasive breast cancer in New Zealand. N Z Med J. 2012;125(1359):7-16. PMID: 22932509.

audits.title: Institutional review of compliance with NCCN guidelines for breast cancer: lessons learned from real-time multidimensional synoptic reporting.
audits.setting: Gundersen Health System, La Crosse, Wisconsin

cycle1.result: Compliance: staging 94%, surgery 97%, chemotherapy 91%, hormone therapy 89%, radiotherapy 91%, follow-up 85%, ER/PR and HER2 100%.

audits.other_findings: Synoptic templated reporting accurate in 97%; main reasons for non-compliance were patient refusal, choice and overuse of testing.

Institutional review of compliance with NCCN guidelines for breast cancer: lessons learned from real-time multidimensional synoptic reporting. audits.title: Clinical auditing as an instrument for quality improvement in breast cancer care in the Netherlands: The national NABON Breast Cancer Audit.
audits.setting: NABON Breast Cancer Audit, all 92 hospitals in the Netherlands

cycle1.result: Pre- and post-operative MDT discussion in 83% and 91%.

audits.intervention: Nationwide clinical audit with hospital benchmarking.

cycle2.result: Pre- and post-operative MDT discussion in 98% and 99%.

audits.other_findings: 56,927 patients in total; re-operation for positive margins stayed low (about 5%); preoperative MRI and immediate reconstruction varied widely between hospitals.

audits.title: Influence of adherence with guideline-driven recommendations on survival in women operated for breast cancer: Real-life evidence from Italy.
audits.standard: Italian Health Ministry quality indicators for breast cancer care (surgery timeliness, medical therapy timeliness, complementary radiotherapy, mammographic follow-up)
audits.setting: Women operated for breast cancer in Lombardy, Emilia-Romagna and Lazio regions (administrative health data)

cycle1.result: Adherence: medical therapy timeliness 53%, mammographic follow-up 73%, surgery timeliness 74%, complementary radiotherapy 82%.

audits.other_findings: Adherence was associated with mortality risk reductions of 26% (medical therapy timeliness), 62% (radiotherapy) and 56% (mammographic follow-up); surgery timeliness showed no effect.
audits.citation: Corrao G, Rea F, Di Felice E, Di Martino M, Davoli M, Merlino L, et al.. Influence of adherence with guideline-driven recommendations on survival in women operated for breast cancer: Real-life evidence from Italy. Breast. 2020;53:51-58. doi:10.1016/j.breast.2020.06.010. PMID: 32629156.

audits.title: Breast cancer care and surgery in Australia and New Zealand: compliance of the BreastSurgANZ quality audit with international standards.
audits.standard: 2017 EUSOMA breast cancer quality indicators and thresholds
audits.setting: BreastSurgANZ Quality Audit prospective population-based database, low- and high-volume hospitals

cycle1.result: Low-volume hospitals met the quality threshold for 10 EUSOMA QIs and high-volume hospitals for 8 (MDT discussion, surgical approach, adjuvant radiotherapy in low-volume hospitals, avoidance of overtreatment, endocrine therapy). Thresholds not met for neoadjuvant chemotherapy use and adjuvant radiotherapy in high-volume hospitals.

audits.other_findings: Data capture completeness needs improvement, including genetic syndrome and Ki67% fields.
audits.citation: Duffield JA, Blanch AJ, Bochner MA. Breast cancer care and surgery in Australia and New Zealand: compliance of the BreastSurgANZ quality audit with international standards. ANZ J Surg. 2023;93(4):881-888. doi:10.1111/ans.18347. PMID: 36856199.

audits.title: Concordance of breast cancer services in an urban tertiary care institute in India to EUSOMA guidelines: An audit of Indian breast cancer practices.
audits.setting: Breast Unit, Max Institute of Cancer Care, New Delhi, tertiary cancer centre

cycle1.result: Clinical assessment, imaging and preoperative work-up met EUSOMA standards; surgery for invasive cancer and DCIS in accordance with guidelines

audits.other_findings: More mastectomies than expected for invasive cancers under 3 cm; neoadjuvant targeted therapy under-used.
